questions.prompt: Explain the purpose of `translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints` and why it must be set to `false` for programmatic Auto Layout.
questions.modelAnswer: By default, views created in code have `translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints` set to `true`. This instructs UIKit to convert legacy autoresizing masks into implicit constraints. When you add custom Auto Layout constraints, these generated constraints conflict with your rules, causing layout collisions. Setting this property to `false` disables legacy masks so your custom constraints can govern the layout.

rubric.criterion: Explains default true converts legacy autoresizing masks into implicit constraints.
Explains setting false prevents conflicting constraint errors with custom anchors.

questions.prompt: Compare Content Hugging Priority and Content Compression Resistance Priority. How do they resolve size conflicts?
questions.modelAnswer: Content Hugging Priority determines how much a view resists stretching larger than its intrinsic content size. When extra space is available, the view with the lower hugging priority stretches to fill the space. Content Compression Resistance Priority determines how much a view resists shrinking smaller than its intrinsic size. When space is constrained, the view with the higher compression resistance avoids text truncation.

rubric.criterion: Explains Content Hugging resists stretching; lower priority stretches to fill extra space.
Explains Compression Resistance resists shrinking; higher priority avoids text truncation.

questions.prompt: Why should iOS developers use `leadingAnchor` and `trailingAnchor` instead of `leftAnchor` and `rightAnchor`?
questions.modelAnswer: In UIKit, `leadingAnchor` and `trailingAnchor` automatically adapt to user language direction. In left-to-right languages like English, leading is left and trailing is right. In right-to-left languages like Arabic and Hebrew, UIKit flips them so leading is right and trailing is left. Using `leftAnchor` and `rightAnchor` locks positions to physical sides and breaks right-to-left localization.

rubric.criterion: Explains leading and trailing flip automatically for right-to-left languages.
Explains left and right remain fixed to physical sides and break internationalization.

questions.prompt: What is `safeAreaLayoutGuide` and why is it important in modern iOS applications?
questions.modelAnswer: `safeAreaLayoutGuide` is a layout guide that defines the portion of a view not obscured by system hardware and bars. It accounts for the top screen notch, the Dynamic Island, the status bar, navigation bars, and the bottom home indicator. Pinning interactive controls to the safe area guide keeps buttons and text accessible and unobstructed across all device models.

rubric.criterion: Defines safe area as the visible screen area unobstructed by hardware notches and bars.
Explains pinning interactive controls prevents obstruction by the Dynamic Island or home bar.

questions.prompt: What causes an `Unable to simultaneously satisfy constraints` error in UIKit and how do you resolve it?
questions.modelAnswer: This error occurs when two or more required constraints with priority 1000 contradict each other, making it mathematically impossible for the solver to satisfy both. For example, constraining a view width to 100 while also pinning both edges to a 200-point parent causes a conflict. To resolve it, lower the priority of one constraint below 1000 (such as 750 or 250), allowing the solver to satisfy the higher priority rule.

rubric.criterion: Explains contradictory required constraints with priority 1000 make solver satisfaction impossible.
Explains lowering one constraint priority below 1000 resolves the conflict gracefully.
